interpretation: Seven baseline-estimation methods are computed independently and their spread indicates sensitivity of the volume estimate to baseline-surface choice. WB sits on a Pleistocene terrace above the floodplain, so a baseline drawn from the full 250 m surrounding ring averages across both upland-terrace and lowland-floodplain pixels and biases the baseline elevation low (inflating volume). The terrace-only and inner-ring methods restrict the baseline to elevations consistent with the terrace surface the site actually sits on. The defensible central estimate for earthwork volume is the terrace-only planar fit (f) or the inner-ring (g) median; the spread across the seven methods serves as a sensitivity range.

refined_per_mound_estimate_m3.method: Per-mound volume integration against local natural-surface baselines. Each mound or mound+ridge group has a baseline drawn from the local minimum elevation in its immediate vicinity (22 m for the K/A/B/C/D, E, and F clusters; 21.5 m for G, H, I, and J + ridge). This avoids the polygon-wide baseline ambiguity of the seven prior methods and assumes the mounds and ridges were built directly on natural ground (no pre-mound surface raising).
refined_per_mound_estimate_m3.supersedes: The prior 15,000-120,000 m³ baseline-method range remains documented below as a sensitivity envelope; the per-mound estimate is the authoritative central value because it uses local rather than polygon-wide baselines and treats the mounds and ridges as resting on natural ground rather than on a constructed inter-mound surface.

recommended_central_estimate_source: Per-mound LiDAR analysis with local natural-surface baselines; see refined_per_mound_estimate_m3 below.
recommended_sensitivity_range_source: Lower bound from terrace-only planar fit (method f above); central from per-mound refined analysis. The full-ring 115k-220k m³ envelope reflects baseline-method ambiguity that the per-mound analysis resolves by using local rather than polygon-wide baselines.
